title: Micro-splitter request pattern lab notes
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick personal lab notes for an extremely small runtime component I prototyped: the "micro-splitter". Goal: client-side (or very-light edge) component that can split a single high-level request into multiple sub-requests optimized for latency/cost/quality tradeoffs, then merge results deterministically. Intended for cases where app wants: A/B response sampling, fast-first-then-best flow, or hybrid heuristics (embedding+ranker + generation).

Key use-cases
- Fast-first-then-best: return a cheap model's answer immediately, then patch in higher-quality result when ready.
- Parallel hypothesis generation: fan-out to different prompt variants or model sizes and choose best via lightweight scorer.
- Trimmed fallbacks: try quantized/low-cost variant concurrently with standard model to reduce tail latency.
- Local heuristic prefilter + remote heavy call: run a small classifier locally to avoid remote call for negative cases.

Non-goals
- Not intended to be full orchestration/orchestration state machine (that's router/ingress job).
- Not for long-running sessions spanning many requests (stateless per request).

Architecture sketch (text)
------------------------
Client App --> Micro-splitter (edge) --> [Branch A: local classifier / cache]
                                        --> [Branch B: lightweight model endpoint (cheap)]
                                        --> [Branch C: heavyweight hosted model]

Splitter responsibilities:
- Interpret a split-config (route-level): which branches, timeouts, retry budgets, scoring rules, merge policy.
- Fan-out in parallel (or staged): manage per-branch deadlines and backpressure.
- Aggregation: apply deterministic merge policy (first-success, majority vote, rank-and-select, diff-apply).
- Emit telemetry spans and per-branch cost/time tags for Console.
- Optional result patching: emit initial response + patch when final arrives (via SSE/webhook).

Config sketch (example JSON as a string here for clarity)
------------------------------------------------------
{
  "split_config_version": "v1",
  "branches": [
    {
      "name": "fast_small",
      "type": "remote_model",
      "model": "gpt-small-q4",
      "timeout_ms": "120",
      "max_tokens": "64",
      "fallback_to": "cheap_cache",
      "sampling": { "temperature": "0.2" }
    },
    {
      "name": "local_filter",
      "type": "inline_fn",
      "handler": "intent-negative-filter",
      "timeout_ms": "20"
    },
    {
      "name": "heavy",
      "type": "remote_model",
      "model": "gpt-medium",
      "timeout_ms": "800",
      "scoring": { "method": "logprob_estimate" }
    }
  ],
  "merge_policy": {
    "primary": "first_non_empty",
    "conflict_resolution": "score_prefers_heavy",
    "patch_delivery": "delta-sse"
  }
}

Behavioral notes
----------------
- Inline functions (inline_fn) run synchronously in the micro-splitter process; keep them < 15ms. Good for token-length heuristics or regex checks.
- Branch timeouts are soft until merge point: if heavy branch finishes after primary returned, splitter emits a patch. Patch semantics must be idempotent on client.
- Score computation: prefer cheap proxies (logprob estimate or short re-ranker) at edge. If branch includes full re-ranker, treat as async.

API shape (ingress -> splitter)
-------------------------------
POST /v1/split-call
Headers: X-Request-Id, Authorization
Body: {
  "prompt": "...",
  "route": "compose/answer-v1",
  "split_config_id": "edge/fast-first-v1",
  "client_pref": { "fast_only": false, "patches_ok": true }
}

Response (fast path)
{
  "request_id": "rdw-abc-123",
  "phase": "initial",
  "payload": { "text": "quick answer...", "branch": "fast_small" },
  "patch_endpoint": "sse://edge/patch/rdw-abc-123"
}

Final patch (if heavy finishes)
{
  "request_id": "rdw-abc-123",
  "phase": "final",
  "payload": { "text": "refined answer...", "branch": "heavy", "confidence_score": "0.82" }
}

Merge policy examples
- first_non_empty: return earliest branch that produced a non-empty answer. Good for latency.
- majority_vote: when several short branches return candidates (e.g., 3 paraphrases), pick the most common.
- best_score: requires a scorer branch that assigns scores, pick highest.
- diff_apply: return fast answer, then apply textual diff from heavy answer as patch. Useful for saving tokens on client display.

Fault and retry semantics (important)
-----------------------------------
- Per-branch retry budgets declared in config. Only idempotent calls allowed for retries.
- If a branch is rate-limited by upstream, fallback to designated fallback branch (from config).
- If heavy branch fails, return a telemetry marker with reason (upstream-502, timeout).
- Splitter must avoid amplifying retries: global per-request cap (e.g., max 5 outgoing calls) and per-route concurrency limiter.

Telemetry & observability
-------------------------
Emit a single trace per user request with child spans per branch. Attach these tags: branch.name, branch.model, branch.duration_ms, branch.cost_estimate_usd, branch.outcome (ok|timeout|error). Aggregate in Console per route to compute added tail-latency and patch frequency.

Local dev experiment plan
-------------------------
- Step 1: implement a minimal splitter as Node process behind local proxy. Accept a JSON split-config and run simple fan-out to two HTTP endpoints (mocked).
- Step 2: add inline_fn handler that can short-circuit negative cases.
- Step 3: implement patch SSE delivery and idempotency checks on client proto (simple sequence number).
- Step 4: collect telemetry, compute patch-rate for a 2k-user synthetic workload.

Open questions (brain dump)
--------------------------
- How to make inline_fn safe? Need WASM sandbox vs Lua vs JS? Security constraints for users uploading functions.
- Should splitter be a library (strong) or a sidecar process (easier rollout)? Tradeoffs: library=lower latency but harder to change; sidecar=config hot-reload.
- How to bill approximate cost? Need per-outbound call estimate. For hosted customers, show estimated extra token cost for split-config.
- How to ensure deterministic merging across retries (idempotence)? Sequence numbers + branch stable ids maybe sufficient.

Short notes to self
-------------------
- Keep inline handlers tiny; prefer precompiled small decision trees.
- Provide a config linter that rejects configs likely to explode (e.g., 10 branches + retries).
- For early prototype, restrict split-config to at most 3 branches.
- Try both SSE and webhook patch delivery; SSE better for browser clients.

References / inspiration
-----------------------
- quick-first-then-best patterns from prior CDN edge ABs
- offline prefilter design in mobile apps (small classifier to reduce calls)
- some notes in Confluence (linked above) that were half-baked

Next actions (personal)
----------------------
- spin up prototype in local env this week, run synthetic workload, capture patch rate and extra cost.
- write a short demo README for product folks showing UX tradeoffs.

-- end --
